newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australia stocks climb back in black by close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks climb back in black by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2416 +2 US 30yr cl 6.87 -0.04
10yrbond futs 92.515 steady Gold NY 345.45 Lon fix 346.80
*Stocks crawl back into black by close, options exercises drive turnover, activity modest. Volume 521.69, A$1.43 bln value, 1,113 traded, 318 steady, 397 up, 398 down.

A mixed Australian share market muddled its way to a firmer close on Friday as Dow-inspired strength in the industrials managed to overcome a resources sector weakened by soft precious and base metals prices.
Option exercises following Thursday's January series expiry inflated otherwise modest turnovers.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 6.0 points at 2,423.7.
March share price index futures were two points higher at 2,416, a 7.7 point discount to the index.

"Commodities, especially gold, kept a large portion of the market down with people still wary," said dealer Peter Struk of Sydney-based brokerage, Reynolds and Co, adding that the impressive-looking volumes belied a reasonably slow day.
"It was large turnover due to options exercises but people really weren't interested today overall," he said.

Individual features came from outside the leaders. In the resources, Cultus Petroleum shares starred, leaping 31 percent to A$1.90 after the company reported oil and gas shows from its Cornea wells offshore Western Australia.

In the industrials, biotechnology group Progen Industries extended its strong gains from Thursday when it announced results from tests of its anti-cancer compound. Its shares closed 18 percent higher at A$1.09.
The half yearly results continue to trickle in with two major base metals miners turning in their reports.
Shares in MIM Holdings shares ended a cent higher at A$1.75 after it posted a net loss of A$12 million for the six months to December 31, compared to a profit of A$58.9 million previously.
North Ltd shares closed two cents higher at A$3.94 after increasing first half net profit by 50 percent to A$50 million.

Junior explorer Carnarvon Petroleum shares topped turnover by volume with 52.9 million shares traded, closing steady at 2.5 cents. The bulk of the activity was in one line of 49.96 million shares crossed at 2.2 cents, with brokers saying 11.29 percent shareholder Devex looked to have sold their stake.
Falls shaded rises by the barest of margins, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade returned to moderate levels after Thursday's frantic expiry-linked activity. Futures trade was at reasonable levels. Total options traded 34,588 (93,990), turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 6,537 (5,040)

In other local markets, Australian bonds put in a lacklustre performance on Friday, shrugging off a firmer tone in U.S. Treasuries and a massive drop in the nation's current account deficit to finish flat to softer across the curve. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10-year T-bonds were yielding 7.40 percent.

The Australian dollar was hounded to fresh 11-month lows Friday as U.S. and Japanese investors dumped it in fear of an imminent rate cut here. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT) the currency had sunk to US$0.7633/38 from an early US$0.7650/55, to be nearly a big figure down on Thursday's late US$0.7710/15.
